metadata.title: SPELLINGBEE
metadata.author: Peter Norvig
metadata.source: Peter Norvig's Spelling Bee Puzzle solution

nodes.name: Spelling Bee Puzzle Game Mechanics
nodes.description: An introduction to the NYTimes Spelling Bee puzzle, outlining its honeycomb letter arrangement, the objective of finding words, and general gameplay constraints.

nodes.name: Valid Word Criteria
nodes.description: The specific rules defining what constitutes a valid word in the Spelling Bee puzzle: minimum length of four letters, inclusion of the central letter, and use of only the seven given letters.

nodes.name: Pangram in Spelling Bee
nodes.description: Definition of a 'pangram' as a valid word that uses all seven letters available in the honeycomb, and the associated bonus points earned for such words.

nodes.name: Word Scoring in Spelling Bee
nodes.description: The point system for words in the Spelling Bee puzzle: 1 point for 4-letter words, word length for longer words, plus a 7-point bonus for pangrams.

nodes.name: Honeycomb Structure Representation
nodes.description: Understanding the honeycomb lattice as a combination of a seven-letter set and a single distinguished center letter, which are crucial attributes for puzzle solving.

nodes.name: Python Basic Syntax
nodes.description: Fundamental Python programming constructs including variables, functions, basic data types (strings, integers, booleans), and control flow.

nodes.name: Python String Operations
nodes.description: Common string manipulation techniques in Python such as converting to uppercase, splitting strings, joining characters, and sorting characters within a string.

nodes.name: Python Set Operations
nodes.description: Key operations on Python sets, including checking if one set is a superset of another (`issuperset`), adding elements, and using set comprehensions for concise creation.

nodes.name: Python List Comprehensions
nodes.description: Using a compact syntax to create new lists by iterating over existing iterables and applying conditions or transformations.

nodes.name: Python Dictionaries
nodes.description: Understanding key-value pairs, dictionary creation, access, modification, and their use as efficient lookup tables.

nodes.name: Python Dataclasses
nodes.description: Utilizing the `dataclass` decorator for easily creating classes primarily used to store data, providing automatic generation of methods like `__init__`, `__repr__`, `__eq__`, and supporting frozen (immutable) instances.

nodes.name: Programmatic Word Filtering
nodes.description: Implementing Python functions to filter a given word list based on specific criteria derived from the puzzle rules, such as minimum length, allowed letters, and exclusion of certain characters.

nodes.name: Representing Lettersets
nodes.description: Exploring different ways to represent unique sets of letters (e.g., sorted strings vs. frozensets) and evaluating their trade-offs in terms of memory usage, readability, and suitability as dictionary keys.

nodes.name: Algorithmic Thinking
nodes.description: The process of designing and analyzing step-by-step procedures to solve computational problems, focusing on problem decomposition, strategy formulation, and efficiency considerations.

nodes.name: Brute-Force Algorithm Design
nodes.description: Designing an algorithm that systematically checks every possible candidate solution to a problem, understanding its directness and inherent high computational cost.

nodes.name: Combinatorial Problem Space Analysis
nodes.description: Analyzing problems involving combinations and permutations to understand the total number of possible arrangements or selections, which helps in estimating the complexity of brute-force solutions.

nodes.name: itertools.combinations for Subsets
nodes.description: Using Python's `itertools.combinations` to efficiently generate all unique combinations (subsets) of elements from a given iterable without repetition.

nodes.name: Constraint-Based Problem Reduction
nodes.description: Applying specific rules or constraints of a problem (e.g., 'must have at least one pangram') to drastically reduce the number of candidates an algorithm needs to consider, moving beyond pure brute force.

nodes.name: Generating Candidate Honeycombs
nodes.description: Programmatically creating all relevant 'Honeycomb' configurations by leveraging pangram lettersets and iterating through each letter as a potential center, significantly narrowing the search space.

nodes.name: Basic Performance Profiling
nodes.description: Using simple tools like IPython's `%timeit` magic command to measure the execution time of code snippets, helping identify performance bottlenecks and evaluate optimization efforts.

nodes.name: Precomputation for Optimization
nodes.description: A general optimization strategy involving performing expensive calculations once, storing their results (e.g., in a lookup table), and reusing these stored results to avoid redundant computations.

nodes.name: collections.defaultdict for Aggregation
nodes.description: Leveraging `collections.defaultdict` to simplify value aggregation in dictionaries by automatically providing a default value for a key if it doesn't exist, reducing boilerplate code.

nodes.name: Points Table Data Structure
nodes.description: An optimized data structure (a dictionary mapping lettersets to aggregated scores) created through precomputation to quickly retrieve total scores for any given letterset, significantly speeding up score calculations.

nodes.name: Calculating Letter Subsets for Scoring
nodes.description: The process of generating all possible subsets of letters from a given honeycomb (ensuring the center letter is always included) to utilize a precomputed 'points table' for faster score calculation.

nodes.name: Upper Bound Calculation for Optimization
nodes.description: A technique to quickly estimate the maximum possible score for a group of candidates (e.g., a pangram letterset regardless of its center) to determine if further detailed computation is necessary, avoiding unproductive search paths.

nodes.name: Branch and Bound Algorithm
nodes.description: An advanced optimization technique that systematically explores a search space, but prunes 'branches' (groups of candidate solutions) if an upper bound calculation indicates they cannot lead to a better solution than the current best found so far.

nodes.name: functools.lru_cache for Memoization
nodes.description: Using the `functools.lru_cache` decorator to automatically cache the results of function calls based on their arguments, thereby avoiding redundant computations for identical inputs (memoization).

nodes.name: Iterative Refinement of Algorithms
nodes.description: A development methodology where an initial simple (e.g., brute-force) algorithm is progressively enhanced and optimized through multiple stages, incorporating advanced techniques like constraint reduction, precomputation, and pruning.

nodes.name: Readability vs. Efficiency Trade-offs
nodes.description: Analyzing the choices made in code design, such as data structure representation or algorithmic approach, weighing the benefits of clear, easy-to-understand code against the need for optimal performance.
